text: Ten thousand volts just jumped from your finger. Why only in winter?
Every step on a carpet, every wool sweater, moves tiny electrons onto or off your body.
That extra charge piles up on your skin, with nowhere to go.
Just walking can charge you to thousands of volts, sometimes over ten thousand.
Then your finger nears metal, and zap! The charge jumps across as a tiny spark.
A mini lightning bolt. Harmless, because it is over in a split second.
In summer, humid air quietly lets that charge leak away.
Winter air is dry, so the charge stays, waiting for the door handle.
Trick: touch metal with a key first. The spark hits the key, not you.
Did a door handle shock you this week? Comment yes or no.
